## Problem

## Requirements

- This is a frontend-focused coding exercise built around React. You'll work against a supplied REST API, making GET, POST, and update calls via `fetch`, parsing the returned data, applying filtering logic, and using basic data structures like `Set`.
- TypeScript is required—expect to both read and write typed code throughout the task.

## Notes

- The API sandbox is intentionally buggy; the interviewer will confirm that it contains defects. You're responsible for writing all the fetch/post/update plumbing from scratch. Study the API contract closely and anticipate producing a substantial amount of code under tight time constraints.
- In at least one interview loop, candidates were given a choice between tracks (for instance, a React track versus an alternative); the React/TypeScript track was consistently described as the more manageable path for frontend engineers.
- Lack of TypeScript fluency was explicitly flagged as a probable failure point for this round. Before the interview, practice writing typed `fetch` wrappers and implementing typed response filtering.

## Solution

The reference solution is on [the question page](https://trueinterview.io/questions/frontend-api-practical), beside an editor that runs your own attempt first. It is not reproduced here — try the problem before you read the answer.
